vorsheinPage.label: Vorshein
vorsheinPage.heading: We don't train swimmers. We build high-performance aquatic capability.
vorsheinPage.intro: VORSHEIN was born from a simple idea: water doesn't forgive improvisation. Anyone who needs to perform in it — for work, physical demand, or personal growth — needs a real preparation system, not a standalone class. That's why VORSHEIN is built as an aquatic performance system, not a traditional swim academy.

control.name: Control
control.text: Before speed, before endurance: control of the body, the breath, and the mind in the water.

endurance.name: Endurance
endurance.text: Endurance isn't improvised. It's built progressively, session after session, with no shortcuts.

performance.name: Performance
performance.text: The end goal is to perform reliably, even — especially — under pressure.

vorsheinPage.methodologyP1: Every participant moves through a three-level system — Foundation, Performance, and Tactical — each one built on real mastery of the last, not on time served. Every person's starting point is determined by Vorshein Assessment, never assumed.
vorsheinPage.methodologyP2Highlight: technique, endurance, breath control, water confidence, speed, underwater performance, recovery, mental control, apnea, and competition preparation
vorsheinPage.methodologyP2Suffix: — are combined according to each person's level and goal.

programDetail.competitionPrepDisclaimer: Indicative structure. The official format for each event is confirmed once the competition calendar goes live.

foundation.duration: 1 cycle: 4 weeks · 8 sessions · Saturday and Sunday
foundation.methodology: Small groups (6 to 10 people) with a dedicated instructor. Every session combines live technical correction, immediate verbal feedback, and measured progression: you don't move to the next skill until the current one is solid. The goal at this stage isn't speed — it's building the confidence and technique that everything after this depends on.
improvements: Real comfort with the face submerged and controlled breathing
Flotation and body balance in the water
Progressive endurance build-up toward the Foundation standard: 102 continuous meters
Managing anxiety in progressively deeper water

breathing.body: At this level the breathing work is foundational, not apnea: bilateral breathing rhythm, controlled exhale underwater, and coordinating breath with stroke. It's the technical base that any real apnea work — later on — is built on.

entryProfile.heading: Entry Profile
entryProfile.intro: Foundation is the entry point for anyone who:
items: Can move in the water without constant assistance
May have technically weak freestyle or backstroke
entryProfile.note: If someone needs constant assistance to stay safely afloat, they currently don't meet GEN 001's minimum entry requirement.

certification.headline: Prove the base.
certification.intro: Completing the 8 sessions doesn't guarantee advancement — Clearance confirms the base is solid.
certification.format: Practical in-water evaluation: a technical checklist covering flotation, breathing, and movement, plus 102 continuous meters without stopping (6 lengths).
certification.retainedNote: If the standard isn't met yet, you repeat the Foundation cycle until you reach it — no extra charge for the Clearance itself.
certification.unlocks: Eligibility to enroll in the Performance program.

performance.duration: 1 cycle: 4 weeks · 8 sessions · Saturday and Sunday
performance.methodology: Interval training with pace plans (splits), video technique analysis, and stroke-specific efficiency work. Breath control under effort is introduced — not competitive apnea, but the ability to hold technique and composure once the body is already fatigued.
improvements: First short static breath-holds, always supervised
Base underwater movement (dolphin kick, body line)

breathing.body: Progressive tolerance to respiratory effort is introduced: short static breath-hold sets (seconds, not minutes), always at the surface, always with a partner actively watching. The goal is familiarity and control, not performance — real high-level apnea belongs to the Tactical program.

underwater.body: Introduction to underwater movement: body line, basic dolphin kick, and short orientation drills without surface visual references. It's the technical base that becomes real dynamic apnea in Tactical.

certification.format: Distance test: 340 meters (20 lengths), with recorded splits at 17 and 34 meters, plus video technique evaluation.
certification.unlocks: Eligibility to request entry evaluation for the Tactical program.

tactical.duration: 1 cycle: 4 weeks · 8 sessions · Saturday and Sunday
tactical.methodology: Individualized periodization based on each participant's load and recovery. Apnea sessions are always supervised 1-on-1 or through a certified buddy system — never solo. Pressure scenarios (fatigue, time limits, decisions under stress) are built in, with video technique review after every block.
improvements: Static apnea: supervised progression of breath-hold time
Dynamic apnea: underwater distance with efficient technique
CO₂ tolerance and oxygen consumption efficiency
Mental control and decision-making under fatigue
Active and passive recovery between high-demand blocks

body: Vorshein's apnea training rests on two real physiological mechanisms. The first is the mammalian dive reflex: submerging the face slows heart rate, redirects circulation toward vital organs, and releases extra red blood cells from the spleen — a natural response that's refined through consistent training.

The second is CO₂ tolerance: the urge to breathe isn't caused by lack of oxygen, it's caused by rising carbon dioxide. That's why training uses progressive tables — CO₂ tables (constant hold time, progressively shorter rests) and O₂ tables (progressively longer holds, constant rest) — under direct supervision in every session.
apnea.safetyNote: Apnea carries a real risk of hypoxia when practiced without supervision. At Vorshein, all apnea training is done with a certified safety observer present at every session, following recognized apnea safety protocols. It is never practiced solo, on or off our premises.

underwater.body: Dynamic apnea with progressive distance, hydrodynamic body position, efficient dolphin kick, and underwater orientation without visual references. Includes equalization technique for depth changes, applicable to both swimming and diving contexts.

competitionPrep.body: A Vorshein evaluation or competition indicatively combines: a timed endurance test, a speed test, static apnea (supervised breath-hold time), dynamic apnea (underwater distance), a technical evaluation, and a physical and mental pressure scenario.

certification.format: Swim test: 510 meters (30 lengths), technical evaluation, and a practical scenario under pressure. Apnea is not a mandatory certification component — it's worked on during training, never as a pass/fail requirement.
certification.unlocks: TACTICAL certification and eligibility for Competition Eligible as soon as the competition calendar goes live.

01.name: Swim Technique
01.description: Efficient swim mechanics: posture, pull, and kick as the foundation for everything else.

02.name: Endurance
02.description: Progressive build of aerobic endurance and the capacity to sustain effort.

03.name: Breath Control
03.description: Conscious management of breathing, on the surface and under effort.

04.name: Water Confidence
04.description: Flotation, controlled immersion, orientation, and position recovery: real autonomy inside the pool, supervised at all times.

05.name: Speed
05.description: Developing power and speed without sacrificing technical efficiency.

06.name: Underwater Performance
06.description: Movement, orientation, and body control below the surface.

07.name: Recovery
07.description: Conscious effort management: breathing recovery and control to sustain technique between sessions.

08.name: Mental Control
08.description: Regulating stress and fatigue to keep decisions clear under pressure.

09.name: Apnea
09.description: Progressive tolerance to breath-holding, always supervised.

10.name: Competition Preparation
10.description: Integrating every prior module into evaluation and competition protocols.

rules.greeting: Hi. I'm Vorshein AI — I can explain the programs, competition requirements, or help you find your level. What do you need?
rules.whatIsThisPage: Vorshein is a high-performance aquatic preparation system — not a traditional swim school. It has three levels (Foundation, Performance, Tactical), a 10-module training manual, and an assessment that gives you a preliminary classification and recommended program.
rules.apneaCompete: Competing requires a TACTICAL classification confirmed in person and reaching Competition Eligible at your Clearance Test. First we need to know your current aquatic level.
rules.compete: Participating in Vorshein competitions requires reaching TACTICAL and Competition Eligible status. Let's start with your preliminary classification via a 2-minute evaluation.
rules.apnea: Apnea training is part of the Tactical program. We can see if that's your starting point with a short evaluation.
rules.experienceHint: With that experience, your starting point is likely Performance. To pin it down precisely, I can start an evaluation that takes about 2 minutes.
rules.level: Vorshein Assessment gives you a preliminary classification — Foundation, Performance, or Tactical — from a short evaluation about your current experience in the water. Your official level is always confirmed in person.
rules.programs: Vorshein has three levels: Foundation (fundamentals), Performance (performance), and Tactical (high performance and apnea). Your assessment determines which one fits you.
rules.philosophy: Vorshein is an aquatic preparation system, not a traditional swim school: control, endurance, and performance under pressure, built progressively.
rules.events: The Vorshein events calendar is launching soon. You can check your competition status anytime in the Events section.
rules.fallback: I'm still in demo mode and didn't quite catch that — I can help with: what Vorshein is, the programs and levels, competition requirements, or how to take your assessment. Which one?
